text.p: Bonds closed firmer with other periphery markets, with futures breaking through an important resistance point at 108.25.

But further progress at the longer end will depend on the foreign trend, particularly in the Bunds, as the 10-year cash seemed reluctant to move below a spread of 90 basis points over the German equivalent, traders said.
The spread closed at 89 basis points against 90 on Monday.
Traders said that they still expected to see an eventual steepening of the curve but some profit-taking by banks who had bought the shorter end a few weeks ago was delaying such a move.
The spread between the March 1999 and the February 2007 bond stood at 112 basis points against 114 at the opening.
The escudo closed stable at 100.52/55 to the mark compared with its 100.50/55 opening.

Some dealers said that the currency had the potential to rise with the approach of the summer, a traditional period of strength, and the looming privatisation of state electricity concern EDP which would draw heavy foreign interest.
